scope: Real PostgreSQL in an isolated local test database and separate Bun scheduler processes. No Box, model or simulated daemon was needed.
checks: SIGKILL a scheduler child while its occurrence INSERT is waiting on an owned advisory checkpoint gate. PostgreSQL rolls back the run and missed window; next_fire_at remains unchanged.
A fresh scheduler child commits one latest-due occurrence, then receives SIGKILL before returning control to a long-lived caller.
Another fresh scheduler process sees no due occurrence at the same instant; accepted run identity and one missed window remain durable.
limits: The schedule instant is fixed for deterministic crash testing. This is not a real-clock or Box execution proof.
The database remains running: separate backup/restore acceptance covers database recovery.
